section.title: Introduction
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.pii finds personally identifiable mentions as exact spans over the original text. A PiiAnnotator writes the opennlp:pii layer from a PiiExtractor; the built-in CursorPiiExtractor recognizes email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, and payment card numbers, each with a type constant and a normalized form. Numeric types are checksum validated, and an IBAN candidate must additionally match the ISO 13616 registry: a registered country code and exactly the length that country assigns, so a checksum-passing run with an unknown country or a wrong length is not reported. An extractor limited to a subset of the types, for a caller that wants only payment data found, is built with new CursorPiiExtractor(Set.of(PiiMention.TYPE_CARD)).

section.title: Annotating and masking
section.para:
A MaskPolicy controls how the covered characters are replaced while staying length preserving. keepingFormat() leaves separators visible so the kind of value stays recognizable, and keepingTrailing(4) leaves the last four letters or digits of each span readable, the customary receipt style. PiiUsageExampleTest asserts the exact output shown here.
String receipt = Masker.mask(document, PiiAnnotator.PII, MaskPolicy.of('*').keepingFormat().keepingTrailing(4)); // "Contact ****@******e.com, call (***) ***-4567, or charge card **** **** **** 1111."
